briefing:
EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
Iran conducted funeral ceremonies for Ayatollah Ali Khamenei amidst varying reports of public attendance and strong calls for revenge, including specific threats against former US President Trump. Meanwhile, critical US-Iran negotiations on nuclear issues and sanctions are set to resume in Pakistan next week, following a temporary pause for the mourning period. Regional tensions remain high, with an Israeli military operation killing a Hezbollah operative in southern Lebanon and continued Israeli strikes targeting Lebanese residential areas.

IRAN
Funeral ceremonies for Ayatollah Ali Khamenei were held in Tehran, with the main prayers led by Ayatollah Jafar Sobhani. Iranian state media claimed massive attendance, citing over 7 million metro trips for mourners, while opposition sources like Al-Arabiya estimated 200,000-300,000 attendees, suggesting significantly lower turnout. During the events, red flags symbolizing revenge were raised, and chants of "Death to America," "Death to Israel," and calls for the "assassination of Trump" were widely reported.

Prominent figures present included Quds Force Commander Ismail Qaani, IRGC Commander Ahmad Vahidi, and representatives from the Houthis. Notably, Mojtaba Khamenei, widely speculated to be the next Supreme Leader, was absent from the funeral prayers, with the New York Times reporting that security officials barred his attendance due to fears of an Israeli assassination attempt or to prevent his location from being compromised. Ali Ozma'ai was officially appointed as the new Commander of the IRGC Navy, replacing Ali Reza Tangsiri, who was reportedly killed in the conflict.

Diplomatically, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi thanked representatives from over 70 countries for attending the funeral and met with Talal Naji, Secretary-General of the Popular Front for the Liberation of Palestine-General Command. Araghchi also confirmed that indirect technical talks between Tehran and Washington in Doha revealed "deep divisions" regarding the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, the release of $6 billion in frozen funds, and a ceasefire in Lebanon. The next round of US-Iran nuclear and sanctions negotiations is scheduled for July 12 in Pakistan.

Militarily, acting Defense Minister warned of a "decisive response" to any violation of the Iran-US ceasefire agreement. IRGC General Yahya Rahim Safavi characterized the conflict with Israel as an "existential war," stating that only one side would remain. The Intelligence Ministry reported dismantling US-Israeli-linked terrorist teams in southeastern Iran. Internally, the New York Times noted a "deep struggle" behind the scenes within the conservative camp to influence the new Supreme Leader's direction. Parliament Speaker Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf is reportedly advocating for negotiations to navigate "horrible two years," contrasting with the Jaleeli faction's calls for immediate revenge. Industries Electronic Shiraz, a facility producing electronic warfare, electro-optic, and avionics equipment, was reportedly targeted in an attack attributed to the US/Israel.

ISRAEL
Israeli forces conducted military operations in southern Lebanon, with reservists of the 551st Brigade identifying and killing an armed Hezbollah operative in the Majdal Zoun area, within Israel's buffer zone, following a manhunt. Division 679 reportedly destroyed a neighborhood in Lebanon where one of its soldiers was severely injured. IDF also utilized artillery in southern Gaza.

Politically, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has requested a meeting with US President Donald Trump at the White House, potentially next week after Trump's NATO summit. Trump remarked, "He knows who's the boss," regarding Netanyahu. MK Yuli Edelstein announced his departure from the Likud party after 23 years, stating an intention to form a new right-wing political framework. Chairman of the Constitution Committee, Simcha Rothman, is advancing legislation to divide and weaken the role of the Attorney General, allowing separate government representation in the High Court and increasing the Justice Minister's oversight. The Tax Authority notified ultra-Orthodox yeshivas that donations would not be tax-exempt if they enroll draft evaders, requesting lists of students. MK Moshe Kinley Tour Paz sought a legal opinion on whether proposed legislation could grant absolute constitutional protection to ultra-Orthodox from military or civil service.

On the home front, the glass doors of the N12 news system in Tel Aviv were shattered by a masked suspect, part of a series of incitement incidents. There is a surge in crime within the Arab society, with a 30-year-old man shot dead in Umm al-Fahm (the 15th murder in a week, 147th this year), and another 17-year-old in Haifa succumbing to gunshot wounds. Investigations in Umm al-Fahm suggest the crime scene was tampered with. Haifa municipality and the Knesset were illuminated in US flag colors to mark the 250th US Independence Day. Released hostage Alon Ohel performed on the USS Nimitz for the US Independence Day celebrations. Far-right minister Itamar Ben-Gvir canceled a planned visit to New York following legal action and grassroots pressure, which was hailed as a victory by the Hind Rajab Foundation.

GAZA & WEST BANK
The IDF engaged in artillery attacks in southern Gaza. Israeli settlers were involved in arson attacks, setting fire to Palestinian farmlands in Turmus Ayya (northeast of Ramallah) and a Palestinian cafe in Wadi al-Sha’ar (south of Nablus). The Hind Rajab Foundation lauded the cancellation of far-right Israeli minister Itamar Ben-Gvir's visit to the US as a "significant victory" in the fight against impunity for Israeli officials accused of war crimes.

LEBANON
An armed Hezbollah operative was killed by IDF reservists from the 551st Brigade in the Majdal Zoun area, within Israel's buffer zone in southern Lebanon, following a manhunt. Israeli forces conducted extensive strikes, with footage showing the detonation of Lebanese residential buildings in Al-Doura (Bint Jbeil), Hadatha, and Tibnin. An air strike was reported in Al-Mansouri, and fires occurred in buildings in Al-Tiri and Deir Sirian. Division 679 of the IDF reportedly destroyed an unspecified neighborhood in Lebanon where one of its soldiers had been severely injured. Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi reiterated Iran's "resolute position" on the necessity for a "definitive end to aggressions" and "complete withdrawal of occupiers from Lebanon." Hezbollah-affiliated Al-Akhbar newspaper reported that US-Iran indirect technical talks in Doha highlighted "deep divisions" on several issues, including a ceasefire in Lebanon. Enemy media estimates place the number of armed operatives south of the Litani River at approximately 1,200.

SYRIA & IRAQ
In Iraq, Muthanna province, along with eight other provinces (Baghdad, Najaf Ashraf, Karbala, Babil, Dhi Qar, Basra, Maysan, Wasit), declared Wednesday and Thursday as official holidays to facilitate public participation in the funeral procession of Ayatollah Ali Khamenei. Iraqi tribal and clan leaders reportedly submitted an official request to Mojtaba Khamenei for the funeral procession to pass through Iraqi territory. In Iraqi Kurdistan, Khorshid Herki was arrested by forces affiliated with Massoud Barzani in Erbil. Subsequently, Kurdistan Counter-Terrorism forces surrounded the homes of the Al-Herki clan in Erbil and arrested several more members. The Iraqi Council of Ministers approved increasing the crude oil allocation in the Iraq-China agreement by 25,000 barrels, opening an account to secure financial commitments for Chinese projects. Reports also indicated "Kurdish gangs" assaulted an Iraqi flag in Erbil. In Syria, security tensions were reported in Salamiyah (eastern Hama countryside) following the kidnapping of several Alawite residents by "Golan gangs," likely referring to Hay'at Tahrir al-Sham or similar extremist groups. Al-Qaeda claimed responsibility for attacks on military positions in Mali, with allied tribal forces also attacking villages against the ruling military junta, though the army claimed the situation was under control.

GULF STATES
The Kuwaiti court sentenced a Kuwaiti citizen to 10 years in prison for alleged connections with Hezbollah. Bahrain's Ayatollah Sheikh Isa Qassem released a statement mourning Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, emphasizing the continued path of Imam Khomeini and Khamenei, and praying for the strength of Iran and the "Axis of Resistance." Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi publicly thanked "true Arab brothers" who participated in Khamenei's funeral. Regarding the Strait of Hormuz, Iran reportedly closed a previously agreed corridor with the United States. Following this, one US E-3B AWACS, six KC-135R, and two KC-46A tanker aircraft were observed flying over the Persian Gulf. Houthi representatives attended Khamenei's funeral, chanting "Death to America" and "Death to Israel." A Houthi official stated that Saudi Arabia's "insistence on suffering losses" indicates its decisions are not its own.

KEY DEVELOPMENTS
1.  **US-Iran Negotiations Advance Amidst Pause:** The next round of US-Iran nuclear and sanctions talks is scheduled for July 12 in Pakistan, following indirect technical discussions in Doha and a one-week pause in hostilities for Ayatollah Khamenei's funeral as announced by President Trump.
2.  **Khamenei Funeral & Revenge Calls:** Ayatollah Ali Khamenei's funeral in Tehran featured strong calls for "revenge" and specific threats to "assassinate Trump," with official attendance figures disputed between state media and opposition sources.
3.  **Mojtaba Khamenei's Absence from Funeral:** Mojtaba Khamenei, widely considered the new Supreme Leader, was notably absent from his father's funeral due to reported security concerns, including fears of Israeli assassination attempts.
4.  **New IRGC Navy Commander:** Ali Ozma'ai was officially appointed to lead the IRGC Navy, replacing Ali Reza Tangsiri, who was reportedly killed in recent hostilities.
5.  **Israeli Operations in Lebanon Intensify:** IDF forces killed an armed Hezbollah operative in Majdal Zoun and reportedly destroyed a neighborhood and detonated residential buildings in multiple locations across southern Lebanon.
6.  **Kuwaiti Citizen Sentenced for Hezbollah Ties:** A Kuwaiti court sentenced a citizen to 10 years imprisonment for alleged connections to Hezbollah.
7.  **Iranian Demand for Israeli Withdrawal from Lebanon:** Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi reiterated Iran's "resolute position" demanding a "definitive end to aggressions" and "complete withdrawal of occupiers from Lebanon."
8.  **Netanyahu-Trump Meeting Scheduled:** Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is slated to meet with US President Donald Trump at the White House next week, following Trump's return from the NATO summit.
9.  **Internal Israeli Political Shift:** MK Yuli Edelstein announced his departure from the Likud party, signaling a new political direction.

THREAT ASSESSMENT
The risk of escalation between Iran, Israel, and the United States remains high. The funeral rhetoric, particularly the explicit calls for revenge and Trump's assassination, combined with the IRGC General Rahim Safavi's "existential war" declaration, indicates a highly volatile stance from factions within Iran. Ongoing Israeli military operations in southern Lebanon, including the killing of a Hezbollah operative and destruction of buildings, are direct flashpoints. The alleged targeting of Iran's Industries Electronic Shiraz points to potential deeper strikes against Iranian strategic infrastructure. The US military presence over the Strait of Hormuz, following Iran's reported closure of a corridor, keeps that waterway a critical flashpoint. Internally, Iran faces potential instability due to a reported power struggle within the conservative camp following Khamenei's death. The upcoming US-Iran negotiations, despite Trump's "one week" pause, occur against a backdrop of deeply rooted mistrust and significant policy differences, particularly regarding the nuclear program and regional security.

REGIONAL & INTERNATIONAL RESPONSE
**United States:** President Trump confirmed a one-week pause in hostilities for Khamenei's funeral, expressing surprise at public mourning but reiterating willingness to negotiate with Iranian leadership. He confirmed an upcoming meeting with PM Netanyahu. Trump also spoke with Russian President Putin, who provided an assessment of the Ukraine war, and with Ukrainian President Zelenskyy. US tactical aircraft conducted flights over the Persian Gulf following Iran's reported closure of a corridor in the Strait of Hormuz.
**Gulf States:** Kuwait has taken action against alleged Hezbollah connections with a prison sentence. Bahrain's Ayatollah Sheikh Isa Qassem voiced support for Iran and the "Axis of Resistance" following Khamenei's death. Houthi representatives attended the funeral, reflecting their alignment with Iran.
**Russia:** President Putin held an hour-and-a-half call with President Trump, discussing the Ukraine war. Russia also announced a joint naval exercise with China in the coming month and claimed to have captured five additional settlements in eastern Ukraine.
**China:** Announced a joint naval exercise with Russia. The Iraqi Council of Ministers also increased its crude oil agreement with China, further solidifying economic ties.
**Turkey:** President Recep Tayyip Erdogan warned of a renewed regional war instigated by Israel, advocating for dialogue and diplomacy to reduce tensions. Turkey is slated to host the upcoming NATO summit.
**European Union:** Russia's Deputy Foreign Minister criticized Europe for its lack of constructive proposals to resolve the Ukraine crisis, while simultaneously calling for Russia's "strategic defeat." Britain and France were criticized by Iran's Deputy Foreign Minister for viewing the Strait of Hormuz as a "stage for military power display." Dozens of UK MPs and members of the House of Lords have called for sanctions against Israeli PM Netanyahu and Justice Minister Yariv Levin over alleged human rights violations against Palestinian detainees.
**Iraq:** Nine provinces declared a holiday for Khamenei's funeral procession, highlighting Iranian influence.

INTELLIGENCE NOTES
**Contradictions and Propaganda:** There are significant, opposing claims regarding the attendance at Ayatollah Khamenei's funeral. Iranian state media reports "millions" and over 7 million metro trips, while opposition and Arab media (Al-Arabiya) estimate 200,000-300,000, calling it "low attendance." This divergence clearly indicates a propaganda battle over public support. President Trump's comment about being surprised by the tears at the funeral, questioning if they were "fake," also falls into this category, appealing to a specific audience.
**Unverified Claims:** The opposition claim that Mojtaba Khamenei has been officially appointed as the new Supreme Leader remains unverified by official Iranian channels, though his absence from his father's funeral fuels such speculation. The claim from 'omid dana' that Foreign Minister Araghchi signed an agreement with Oman to divide the Strait of Hormuz, allowing European access and removing Iran's protest rights, lacks corroboration and is likely a propaganda effort designed to undermine the Iranian regime's image. Similarly, the specific details of Industries Electronic Shiraz being attacked by US/Israel are from a less authoritative source.
**Reporting Gaps:** The specific location of the "neighborhood in Lebanon" reportedly destroyed by IDF Division 679 is not provided. Details on the "terrorist teams" dismantled in southeastern Iran, beyond their "US-Israeli link," are sparse. The exact nature and perpetrators of the "Golan gangs" operating in Syria are not specified, although the context suggests anti-regime or extremist elements. There is no clear operational detail on how "Iran closed a corridor" in the Strait of Hormuz, or its immediate practical implications for shipping. The identities of the victims in the Umm al-Fahm and Dir Hanna murders in Israel are not mentioned.
